summary: postinstall auto-executes opaque Go binary that mismatches shipped C source and README
details: On npm install, scripts/postinstall.js invokes nativeBinaryPath() from src/hint.js and immediately runs prebuilt/linux-x64/sudoku-hint via execFileSync(bin, ['--selftest']) on Linux x64 hosts. The shipped Linux binary is a 33,976,468-byte stripped Go executable (sha256 ac6b4523fbe02c79129e58bdc8d613ddfb3a786c23dd03fa4ab28ab38ff3e6e5) containing Go runtime markers (runtime., reflect., chacha8, GODEBUG=, maps.Map, [bisect-match). The only shipped native source is native/hint.c (C, ~200 lines), which cannot produce a Go binary; the darwin-x64 counterpart compiles from that C source to ~13 KB Mach-O, whereas the Linux artifact is ~34 MB. The README additionally claims the Linux binary is 'ELF, statically linked against musl, 26 KB' — materially false. There is no reproducible build path from the shipped source to the executed Linux bytes, so the code that runs on Linux installers at install time cannot be verified against any reviewable source in the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
